title: Mode
body:
The most frequently occurring value. **The only measure of central tendency that works on
qualitative data**, since finding the most common eye colour needs no arithmetic, and the only one
that need not be unique: a dataset can be bimodal (two peaks) or have no mode at all if every value
occurs once.

Bimodality is the useful signal here. Two modes usually means two populations got mixed together,
and no single centre describes the result. A [[Descriptive Statistics|histogram]] shows it
immediately where a [[Mean]] hides it.

For a continuous [[Random Variable]] the mode is the argmax of the
[[Probability Density Function|density]], which is where the [[Normal Distribution]]'s mode,
median, and mean all coincide at $\mu$.

## Related

- [[Average Value]], [[Mean]], [[Median]]
- [[Descriptive Statistics]]: skew is read off the order $\text{mode} < \text{median} < \text{mean}$
